title: Othello and Iago
text:
Othello, a Moorish general in the service of Venice, had secretly married Desdemona, a senator's daughter, who loved him for the dangers he had passed. His ensign Iago, resentful that Othello had promoted Michael Cassio over him, set out to destroy them all, while appearing to be the most honest man in the army.

Iago worked by suggestion. He got Cassio drunk and disgraced, then urged him to ask Desdemona to plead for him. Meanwhile he dropped hints to Othello: how close Cassio and Desdemona seemed, how she had deceived her own father. He never accused outright; he let Othello's imagination do the work. When Desdemona innocently pleaded for Cassio, every word looked like proof.

Then Iago's wife Emilia found a handkerchief Othello had given Desdemona as his first gift, and gave it to her husband. Iago planted it in Cassio's room and let Othello see Cassio with it. Othello, consumed by jealousy, no longer trusted his wife's denials, only Iago's lies.

That night Othello smothered Desdemona in her bed. Emilia, discovering the murder, revealed the truth about the handkerchief, and Iago killed her. Othello understood too late that he had believed a liar over the woman who loved him. He called himself one who loved not wisely but too well, and stabbed himself, while Iago was led away to torture, refusing to say another word.
lesson: Be careful whose suggestions you let shape your view of the people closest to you. Before acting on suspicion, ask them directly.
